title: Anxiety in Parkinson's
content: Anxiety can occur in people with Parkinson's disease, but anxiety can also occur independently and does not mean that someone has Parkinson's. A person may describe feeling anxious, panicked, nervous, worried, frightened, restless, overwhelmed or unable to calm down. Anxiety can also cause physical sensations such as a racing heartbeat, sweating, trembling, dizziness, shortness of breath or chest discomfort. A panic attack can involve a sudden episode of intense fear or panic with strong physical symptoms. Anxiety in someone with Parkinson's may be influenced by symptoms, changes in brain chemistry, medication fluctuations or concerns about living with the condition. Anxiety or panic symptoms alone do not indicate Parkinson's disease. Persistent or recurring anxiety that interferes with everyday life should be discussed with a healthcare professional. Severe or unusual symptoms should not automatically be assumed to be anxiety.
